summary: Israeli forces killed a Hamas commander in Deir al-Balah who was involved in tunnel restoration and terror plot advancement. Multiple drone strikes occurred in southern Lebanon targeting areas between Bint Jbeil and Rachaya. Cyberattacks attributed to Iran targeted British infrastructure and Israeli facilities, with reports of a four-day power station outage in the UK.

sections.threat_assessment: The conflict is experiencing multi-domain escalation with kinetic operations expanding into southern Lebanon and cyber warfare targeting critical infrastructure. Hamas tunnel restoration activities indicate attempts to reestablish underground capabilities despite ongoing operations. Iranian cyber operations represent a significant non-kinetic threat vector that could disrupt regional stability and critical services.
sections.regional_response: International responses include British government confirming cyberattack impact without affecting public grid, while French and British diplomatic warnings issued regarding Israeli military actions in Lebanon. Iraqi political discourse focuses on weapons seizure issues and regional security concerns. Regional public discourse reflects economic disparities and fuel subsidy debates in Iran.
sections.intelligence_notes: Cyber operations attributed to Iran show increasing sophistication with successful penetration of British infrastructure. Drone technology deployment suggests experimental capabilities testing. Cross-border operations in Lebanon indicate expanding operational scope beyond traditional Gaza-Israel axis. Intelligence gathering on tunnel restoration activities provides insight into Hamas operational resilience.
